newsitem.title: UK: Somerfield yr profits to rise, sales eyed.
newsitem.headline: Somerfield yr profits to rise, sales eyed.

text.p: British second-tier supermarket group Somerfield Plc should turn in a rise in year profits when it reports on July 17 but analysts expect sales to be disappointing as the chain struggles against the might of the market leaders.

"Greatest concern is looking at the sales line. Lots of profit growth has come from gross margin and cutting operating costs and Somerfield can't keep that going indefinitely," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.

Somerfield, reporting its first annual results since flotation in August 1996, is expected to turn in pretax profits between 101.5 and 105.0 million stg, compared with proforma profits a year ago of 91.8 million stg, and pay out a dividend of 10.0 to 10.3 pence per share.
Same-store sales are widely expected to be at most around one percent higher with some analysts predicting a fall as low price inflation also takes its toll.
That would mean a slowdown from the four percent rise in same-store sales recorded in the first nine weeks of the second half over the key Christmas period.
"Somerfield is running hard to stand still," said Clive Black of Charterhouse Tilney.
Somerfield is Britain's fifth biggest retailer behind the leaders Tesco, J. Sainsbury, Safeway and ASDA.
It was created in one of the big leveraged buyouts of the 1980s and is in the process of converting its old Gateway stores into the new-style Somerfield format.
Analysts said sales at the old Gateway stores waiting to be converted and the Food Giant discount chain were likely to be weaker than at the core group, providing a drag on overall sales.
"Somerfield is not in a desperately happy position, fending off the big four, but then it's not very highly rated so there's little expectation," the analyst said.
Shares in the group, however, were setting new highs on Friday as food retailers benefited from renewed buying interest.
Somerfield, which is on a lower rating than the leading sector stocks, was trading at 193 pence at 1000 GMT, just off a year high of 194 set earlier and up 5.5 pence.

The group was floated at 145 pence, a level which had to be cut twice, once from an initial offer of 180-190 pence and then from 160 pence as it debuted on a market flooded with new issues. -- Jo Winterbottom, London Newsroom +44171 542 7717
